why: From A to B all parts move into one column on the right. The arrow sign turns 135 degrees anticlockwise and its dot turns with it, the trapezium turns upside down, and the stick with the ball turns a quarter turn clockwise. Apply the same to C: the arrow ends pointing down-right with the dot on its left, the trapezium becomes wide at the bottom, and the ball goes to the right end of the stick. Option 3 matches all of this. Option 5 has the dot on top, and option 1 keeps the trapezium upside down.
trick: When a figure has three or four small parts, follow each part separately and remove options that fail even one part.
note: Figure C is partly covered by handwriting in the scan; C is redrawn from the visible parts and the rule. The stick at the bottom of option 3 is also scribbled over; drawn with the ball on the right (as the rule needs).
